note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF campground just off the Snowy Range Scenic Byway (WY-130), 7.8 miles west of Centennial at the Brooklyn Lake Road (FR 317). Reopened after beetle-kill clearing, so little shade; Nash Fork Creek runs along the east side. Brooklyn Lake and its trail network are 3 miles north. --Claude
summary: FS + rec.gov 10250599 read: 23 sites (count 24 -> 23), 11 reservable / 12 FCFS, $20, no water or hookups, 3 vault toilets, 14-day limit, 8 people; FS 'trailers up to 22 feet' (passes under the 22-ft ruling; max_rig_ft 25 -> 22). Season stored manual closes 10-10 left (rec.gov last first-come night 09-28 - flagged). Not waterfront kept; creekside lead on sites 01-02.
flags: FIT (criteria, report): FS 'Can accommodate trailers up to 22 feet.' - passes under the AWH 2026-10-20 22-ft ruling; rec.gov driveways 26-99 ft. max_rig_ft 25 (derived, unsourced) -> 22.

SEASON CONFLICT (manual value, not overwritten): stored season closes 10-10 (manual, 2026-11-08 from the FS 'Early October'). rec.gov's 2026 seasons run 06-05 to 09-28 (first-come before 07-03 and after 09-12). The FS page itself says both 'Open season is early June to early October' and 'Seasons of Use Early July ... - Early October'. The stored closes 10-10 has no opens; rec.gov says early June (06-05 in 2026).

WATERFRONT LEAD: rec.gov lists 'Creek Access' and the FS says the creek meanders 'through the campground'. On imagery Nash Fork Creek is a narrow willow-lined trickle on the east side, ~25-35 m from the east-spur sites 02 (41.35902,-106.23457) and 01 (41.35858,-106.23453), over open burned ground for 02 (the loop road lies between 01 and the creek). The catalog tags no site for water. Not upgraded: the stream is tiny and the catalog points and pads don't line up exactly on the imagery; not waterfront kept.
